newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal funds may invest 100 bln esc in EDP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal funds may invest 100 bln esc in EDP.

text.p: Portuguese investment and pension funds could potentially invest more than 100 billion escudos in next month's privatisation of state electricity utility Electricidade de Portugal (EDP), according to fund management associations.

Investment funds could apply for EDP shares up to a limit of around 20 billion escudos and pension funds could invest up to 100 billion escudos in the privatisation which is due to take place on June 16.

Jose Carlos Maia of the Portuguese Association of Investment Fund Managers (APFIN) said that at the end of April investment funds held 135 billion escudos in shares. He said that fund holdings in any one company were limited to 10 percent of the total portfolio.
Rui Correia Pedras of the Association for Pension Fund Managers said pension funds could invest up to 100 billion escudos in the electricity firm.
Pension funds are limited to five percent stakes of the total of any one company but, in certain circumstances, this limit can be raised to 10 percent.
"Given that some pension funds already hold investments in EDP bonds, I think that in practice they won't go up to 10 percent. I think seven percent would be a more realistic maximum," Pedras said.
"A total of 100 billion escudos (for pension fund stakes in EDP) seems high but 60 to 70 billion would be a low estimate," he said.
The government on Thursday set a privatisation price of 1,750-2,250 escudos ($1.02-1.32) per share for the partial privatisation of EDP.

The privatisation should raise up to 400 billion escudos, if the state floats between 20 and 30 percent of the company, although the exact percentage to be sold will be set early next month. It will be the biggest state sale ever carried out in Portugal.
